government.note: Parliamentary constitutional monarchy with a ceremonial monarch. The government depends on the confidence of the unicameral Storting, which cannot be dissolved early. On 1 January 2000 Kjell Magne Bondevik led a KrF-Sp-V minority coalition (42 of 165 seats) formed after the 1997 election; the 1997 election article says it relied on support from the Conservative and Progress parties. It resigned in March 2000 and Labour's Jens Stoltenberg took over.

holders.note: Reigned until his death on 28 August 2026. Crown Prince Haakon acted as regent for several periods (2003-2004, 2005, 2020, 2024 and 18-28 August 2026); these regencies are not recorded as separate tenures.

offices.note: Heirs are listed as on 1 January 2000: Crown Prince Haakon, then Princess Märtha Louise (Haakon took precedence under the male-preference rule that applied to Harald V's children; absolute primogeniture applies to later generations). Haakon's daughter Ingrid Alexandra, born 2004, became heir apparent on his accession.

system.note: Modified Sainte-Laguë in 19 multi-member constituencies (the former counties) plus national levelling seats, for which a party needs 4% nationally. The chamber had 165 seats until the 2005 election and 169 since. Until 2009 the elected Storting divided itself into the Lagting (a quarter of members) and the Odelsting for passing laws ('qualified unicameralism'); the 2007 amendment ending this took effect with the Storting elected in 2009. It is modelled as one chamber throughout. seats_2000 is the 1997 election result; mid-term changes before 1 January 2000 were not checked.
